script.text: Eighty-one billion dollars, the biggest stock listing ever. What is Claude's maker worth now?

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude A.I. models, priced its shares at eighty-three dollars late Wednesday. That is above its range of seventy to seventy-eight. CNBC and Axios report the sale raised about eighty-one billion dollars. Nasdaq trading starts Thursday.

That tops SpaceX, which raised about seventy-five billion in June, CNN reports. Saudi Aramco raised about twenty-nine billion in twenty nineteen. Strong demand let Anthropic sell about nine hundred eighty million shares, up from eight hundred twenty-five million planned.

What is it worth? At eighty-three dollars, reports put Anthropic at about one point five trillion dollars, counting all shares. Its last private round valued it at nine hundred sixty-five billion. Seven tech firms, including Nvidia, are also buying twenty-six billion privately.
Will Anthropic's stock end its first week above eighty-three dollars? Yes or no?

upload.title: Anthropic Raises $81 Billion in Record Stock Debut #shorts
upload.description:
Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, priced its IPO at $83 per share on November 18, 2026, above its marketed range of $70 to $78. CNBC and Axios report the offering raised about $81.3 billion, the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX's roughly $75 billion listing in June. At the IPO price, reports put the company's fully diluted value at about $1.5 trillion; shares begin trading on Nasdaq on November 19 under the ticker ANT. Seven tech companies agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting stock in a concurrent private placement. Not investment advice.

Sources: CNBC, Axios, CNN, NPR, ABC News, Yahoo Finance, Washington Times, Anthropic S-1 filing (via coverage).
